title: Meet a pipeline
summary: A pipeline is a saved sequence of build or check steps. Jenkins can run it and keep a record of the result.
introduction: A pipeline is a saved sequence of build or check steps. Jenkins can run it and keep a record of the result. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A pipeline is a saved sequence of build or check steps. Jenkins can run it and keep a record of the result.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These are Jenkins Pipeline examples and fragments. Use the current official setup requirements if you later create a local disposable Jenkins installation. Nothing runs on this tutorial site.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Jenkins. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.title: Meet a pipeline

blocks.text: This declarative Jenkinsfile contains one stage that prints a message. It does not deploy anything.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Find the stage name and the step.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Jenkins is a separate automation tool; this learning app does not need a Jenkins server.
For more detail later, use this [Jenkins further reading](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/).

seo.title: Jenkins: Meet a pipeline
seo.description: Learn about meet a pipeline in Jenkins. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
